description: Guide a student to build a walk-forward validation framework on top of a backtest engine for a parameterized BTCUSDT moving-average crossover strategy, using rolling train and test windows with out-of-sample reporting.

student_openings.beginner_no_finance: I tried different moving average settings and found one that works amazingly well. But I'm worried I just got lucky. Is there a way to properly test whether my parameters are actually good?
student_openings.intermediate_developer: I want to build a walk-forward optimization framework for my backtester. I understand rolling train and test windows, but I'm not sure how to structure it cleanly on top of my existing engine.
student_openings.advanced_quant: I need a walk-forward validation harness for my futures backtest engine. I want to systematically test whether my optimized parameters generalize. What's the cleanest architecture?

ground_truth.expected_outcome: Tutor guides the student to build a walk-forward validation framework that splits data into rolling windows with configurable train and test sizes, runs multiple parameter combinations per training window, applies best parameters to out-of-sample test periods, aggregates OOS results, and reports in-sample versus out-of-sample metrics showing any overfitting gap. The tutor explains why walk-forward validation helps prevent overfitting compared to simple train-test splits. The run should leave concrete walk-forward artifacts such as per-window results, best-parameter records, and explicit IS versus OOS summaries.
required_capabilities: Implement rolling-window data splitting with configurable train and test sizes
Build a parameter optimization loop that runs multiple backtests per training window
Apply optimal parameters to out-of-sample test periods
Aggregate and report in-sample versus out-of-sample performance separately
Explain why walk-forward validation helps prevent overfitting
